bugs.name: Select all monitors leaves expanded group children unchecked
bugs.summary: Select all monitors selects parent groups but leaves visible child monitors unchecked.
bugs.expected: Select all should select the group and its child monitors.
bugs.actual: Select all monitors selects parent groups but leaves visible child monitors unchecked.
reproSteps: Sign in to Uptime Kuma and create a disposable monitor group with at least one child monitor if none exists.
Expand the group in the dashboard.
Click Select all monitors and inspect the child checkbox and selected count.
Deselect all monitors afterward.

bugs.name: HTTP(S) monitor Domain Exp. summary renders Invalid Date
bugs.summary: A newly created HTTP(S) monitor with Domain Name Expiry Notification enabled displays Invalid Date in Domain Exp. after its first check.
bugs.expected: Domain Exp. should display a valid date after the monitor check.
bugs.actual: A newly created HTTP(S) monitor with Domain Name Expiry Notification enabled displays Invalid Date in Domain Exp. after its first check.
reproSteps: Create a disposable HTTP(S) monitor pointed at the fixture URL with Domain Name Expiry Notification enabled.
Wait for the first check and inspect Domain Exp. on the monitor detail.
Delete only the disposable monitor afterward.

bugs.name: Select-all checkbox stays checked after the only selected row is unchecked
bugs.summary: The header select-all checkbox remained checked after the only filtered monitor row was unchecked, while the selection count and bulk-action controls disappeared. The state persisted after five seconds; the new monitor was deleted after verification.
bugs.expected: After unchecking the only selected row, the select-all checkbox should be unchecked and no monitors should be selected.
bugs.actual: With the exact-name search returning one row, selecting all showed “selected: 1.” Unchecking that row visibly cleared its checkbox and removed the selection count and bulk-action controls, but the header checkbox remained visibly checked.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture admin, create a disposable HTTP(S) monitor aimed at http://uptime-kuma:3001/, and search for its exact name so it is the only visible sidebar row.
Click the header select-all checkbox and confirm the row is checked and the UI says selected: 1.
Uncheck the row. Observe the row and selection count clear while the header select-all checkbox remains checked.

bugs.name: Manual monitor Down action creates it before Save
bugs.summary: On the Add New Monitor form, clicking Down for a new Manual monitor immediately persists the monitor and navigates to its detail page, bypassing Save.
bugs.expected: Choosing an initial manual status should not persist a new monitor until Save is clicked.
bugs.actual: After entering a unique Friendly Name and choosing Manual, clicking Down navigates from /add to /dashboard/5. The new monitor is already present in the sidebar with a Down check; Save was never clicked.
reproSteps: Sign in to Uptime Kuma and open Add New Monitor.
Select Manual and enter a unique Friendly Name.
Click Down without clicking Save.
Observe navigation to a new /dashboard/{id} page and the newly created Down monitor in the sidebar.

bugs.name: 1w response-time chart omits available readings
bugs.summary: The response-time chart consistently becomes empty when the range is set to 1w, despite showing recent readings in 24h.
bugs.expected: With 1w selected, the response-time chart should include the monitor readings visible in 24h because those readings fall within the selected one-week period.
bugs.actual: The recent response chart plotted several readings, but the 1w range showed axes and no plotted values.
reproSteps: Open the seeded Admin Sign-in Page monitor, which has several recorded response times.
View the recent response chart and switch its range to 1w.
Observe that the 1w chart has axes but no plotted readings, although recent readings fall within the week.

bugs.name: Websocket Upgrade uses a WebSocket URL scheme as the Friendly Name placeholder
bugs.summary: Websocket Upgrade uses a WebSocket URL scheme as the Friendly Name placeholder
bugs.expected: The Friendly Name field uses a prompt that indicates a monitor name should be entered.
bugs.actual: The Friendly Name placeholder is “wss://”, the WebSocket URL scheme, matching the URL field placeholder rather than suggesting a friendly name.
reproSteps: Open Add New Monitor and select Websocket Upgrade.
Observe that the Friendly Name input has wss:// as its placeholder.

bugs.name: Browser monitor Screenshot Delay is blank in Edit after saving
bugs.summary: A browser monitor saved with a 2500 ms Screenshot Delay shows that field blank in Edit immediately after saving and after reloading.
bugs.expected: The Edit form should show the configured Screenshot Delay of 2500 ms after saving and continue to show it after reloading.
bugs.actual: The Add form showed 2500 ms, but the Screenshot Delay field was blank in Edit both immediately after saving and after a page reload. The monitor name and URL remained populated.
reproSteps: Create a disposable HTTP(s) Browser Engine monitor and set Screenshot Delay to 2500 ms.
Save the monitor and open Edit.
Observe that the Screenshot Delay input is blank while the name and URL remain populated.

bugs.name: RabbitMQ username label repeats “RabbitMQ”
bugs.summary: RabbitMQ username label repeats “RabbitMQ”
bugs.expected: The username field label should identify the RabbitMQ username once, such as “RabbitMQ Username.”
bugs.actual: The visible username field label reads “RabbitMQ RabbitMQ Username.”
reproSteps: Open Add New Monitor and select RabbitMQ.
Observe that its username field label reads RabbitMQ RabbitMQ Username.

bugs.name: gRPC Keyword monitor surfaces null-property exception for unresolved endpoint
bugs.summary: A fresh gRPC Keyword monitor for an unresolvable .invalid endpoint is marked Down, but its visible alert and check message expose a null-property JavaScript exception instead of an endpoint-resolution or connection error.
bugs.expected: The monitor should report the failed endpoint resolution or connection in its Down alert, without exposing a raw null-property JavaScript exception.
bugs.actual: The monitor was marked Down. Its heartbeat message and red alert displayed “Cannot read properties of null (reading 'toString')” (the alert included the monitor name and [DOWN]). The alert remained visible after waiting and appeared again after reopening the monitor details, ruling out a stale one-off toast.
reproSteps: Create a disposable gRPC(s) Keyword monitor with a hostname ending in .invalid, a keyword, and Health/check fields; leave Proto Content blank.
Save and open its details.
Observe the Down alert and heartbeat message Cannot read properties of null (reading toString).

bugs.name: gRPC Health.Check monitor fails with service[method] is not a function
bugs.summary: A newly saved gRPC Keyword monitor configured for Health.Check reports the internal error “service[method] is not a function” instead of an endpoint-reachability or configuration error.
bugs.expected: With the configured Health.Check proto, the monitor should not fail with an internal method-call exception. Since the endpoint uses the reserved .invalid domain, any failure should indicate endpoint reachability or provide a clear configuration-validation message.
bugs.actual: After saving, monitor #108 displayed Down and both its visible alert and history row reported “service[method] is not a function.” The alert remained visible after six seconds.
reproSteps: Create a disposable gRPC(s) Keyword monitor with Health/Check and a valid proto3 definition of the Check RPC; use an unreachable .invalid endpoint.
Save and open its details.
Observe the Down alert and heartbeat message service[method] is not a function rather than a connection or validation error.

bugs.name: Tags filter menu clips option counts at mobile viewport width
bugs.summary: On the 390×844 mobile dashboard, opening Tags after searching for “Admin Sign-in” leaves the right-aligned option counts clipped beyond the viewport, even after the menu settles.
bugs.expected: At 390×844, the Tags filter menu should fit within the viewport so each tag option and its count can be read without horizontally scrolling the page.
bugs.actual: The opened menu extends past the right edge of the 390px viewport, cutting off the right-aligned count values. The clipping persisted after a six-second wait. Horizontally scrolling the page shifted the menu enough to reveal the counts, and scrolling back restored the clipping.
reproSteps: Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels, load the supplied saved administrator session, and open /dashboard.
Select the bottom List navigation tab.
Enter “Admin Sign-in” in the monitor search field.
Open the Tags filter menu.

Observe that the menu extends past the right edge and the full counts are not visible; wait six seconds and observe that the clipping remains. Horizontally scroll the page to reveal the counts, then scroll back and observe the clipping return.

bugs.name: Clearing Heartbeats leaves old latency and uptime statistics displayed
bugs.summary: Clear Data > Heartbeats updates the monitor to Unknown but leaves average latency and uptime statistics from the deleted heartbeats until the page is reloaded.
bugs.expected: Clearing Heartbeats immediately resets the displayed aggregate statistics to values reflecting the empty history.
bugs.actual: Status becomes Unknown and current response N/A, but average response remains 2ms and all uptime cards remain 100%. Reload resets average response to N/A and uptime to 0%. Reproduced twice on the test monitor.
reproSteps: Sign in and open an HTTP monitor with at least one successful heartbeat and nonempty average response/uptime statistics.
Pause the test monitor and confirm Yes.
Click Clear Data, choose Heartbeats, and confirm Yes.
Wait five seconds and compare status, current response, average response and uptime.
Reload the monitor details.

bugs.name: New WebSocket monitors default to HTTP status codes and mark healthy endpoints Down
bugs.summary: Selecting Websocket Upgrade on a fresh monitor keeps the HTTP default accepted codes 200-299, which cannot accept a normal WebSocket close code 1000 and causes a false outage.
bugs.expected: New WebSocket monitors default to an appropriate successful WebSocket status such as normal closure 1000.
bugs.actual: The default configuration marks the endpoint Down with 'Unexpected status code: 1000'. Changing only Accepted Status Codes to 1000 changes it to Up with '1000 - OK'. Reproduced on two newly created monitors.
reproSteps: Sign in and click Add New Monitor.
Select Websocket Upgrade.
Enter a name and a working WebSocket URL. Verified with ws://localhost:3001/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=websocket on this deployment.
Leave Accepted Status Codes at the default 200-299 and save.
Edit the monitor, replace 200-299 with 1000, and save without changing the URL.

bugs.name: SNMPv3 monitor discards its username on Save
bugs.summary: The SNMP monitor editor loses the entered SNMPv3 username on creation and edit while preserving other configuration, preventing the selected identity from being used. Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): SNMPv3 Username is visibly accepted and the form reports Saved, but the value is absent after the monitor edit form reloads. Count this as the same reference rather than a separate bug.
bugs.expected: The entered SNMPv3 username persists after saving and reopening.
bugs.actual: Version 3, OID and query values are preserved, but Username is empty. Editing and saving another username clears it immediately, and a full reload still shows an empty field.
reproSteps: Sign in, click Add New Monitor, and select SNMP.
Enter a name, hostname 127.0.0.1, port 1, Community public, and OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0.
Select SNMP Version 3, enter Username qa, and Expected Value 1.
Save and reopen the monitor using Edit.
Enter Username qa-snmp-user, save again, and reload the editor.
Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): Load the supplied authenticated administrator session and navigate to /add.

Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): Create a fresh monitor named mc-proto-net-snmp-v3-repro-20260616-7e91. Select SNMP; enter Hostname 127.0.0.1, Port 161, Community String public, OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0; select SNMPv3 and enter mc-proto-net-snmp-user as the SNMPv3 Username. Set Json Query Expression to $ and Expected Value to test, then click Save.
Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): Open the newly created monitor's detail view and click Edit. The username field is empty after this initial save.
Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): Enter mc-proto-net-snmp-user in the SNMPv3 Username field and click Save. The UI displays a Saved confirmation.
Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): Refresh /edit/140 and wait for the edit form to finish loading. The SNMPv3 Username field is empty and shows its placeholder.

Reported variant (mo-30m-uptime_kuma-12): For a falsification check, type mc-proto-net-snmp-user into the field using normal keyboard typing, click Save, refresh the same Edit page, and wait for it to load. The field is again empty.

reviewedVariants.name: SNMPv3 Username Is Not Persisted After Saving Monitor
reviewedVariants.summary: SNMPv3 Username is visibly accepted and the form reports Saved, but the value is absent after the monitor edit form reloads.
reviewedVariants.expected: After saving the SNMP monitor and refreshing its Edit form, the SNMPv3 Username field should retain mc-proto-net-snmp-user.
reviewedVariants.actual: The Edit form showed a Saved confirmation after submitting the username, but after refresh and form load the SNMPv3 Username input was empty and showed its placeholder. Repeating the entry using normal keyboard typing produced the same result.
reproSteps: Load the supplied authenticated administrator session and navigate to /add.

Create a fresh monitor named mc-proto-net-snmp-v3-repro-20260616-7e91. Select SNMP; enter Hostname 127.0.0.1, Port 161, Community String public, OID 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1.0; select SNMPv3 and enter mc-proto-net-snmp-user as the SNMPv3 Username. Set Json Query Expression to $ and Expected Value to test, then click Save.
Open the newly created monitor's detail view and click Edit. The username field is empty after this initial save.
Enter mc-proto-net-snmp-user in the SNMPv3 Username field and click Save. The UI displays a Saved confirmation.
Refresh /edit/140 and wait for the edit form to finish loading. The SNMPv3 Username field is empty and shows its placeholder.
For a falsification check, type mc-proto-net-snmp-user into the field using normal keyboard typing, click Save, refresh the same Edit page, and wait for it to load. The field is again empty.

bugs.name: Zero latency is displayed as unavailable instead of 0 ms
bugs.summary: Push monitor details treat numeric zero as missing data: current ping and an all-zero average display N/A, even though zero is included in later averages.
bugs.expected: A recorded zero latency displays 0ms or <1ms; an average of zero-valued samples is displayed as zero, not unavailable.
bugs.actual: After the first zero heartbeat, the monitor is Up but both current and average Ping display N/A. Sending 7 displays current7ms and average3.50ms, proving the zero sample exists. Sending zero again changes current Ping back to N/A, which persists after reload.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a Push monitor.
Open its generated Push URL with a single ping=0 query parameter and status=up.
Inspect current Ping and Avg. Ping with this initial successful heartbeat.
Send another heartbeat with ping=7, then another with ping=0.
Reload the monitor details.

bugs.name: Kafka Producer saves without any broker
bugs.summary: The Kafka Producer form accepts an empty broker list and creates a monitor that immediately fails because it has no broker to connect to.
bugs.expected: Saving is blocked with validation requiring at least one Kafka broker.
bugs.actual: The form reports Added Successfully and opens the created monitor, which immediately reports Down with 'Error in producer connection: Failed to connect: brokers array is empty'. Reproduced on two separate monitors (/dashboard/16 and /dashboard/17).
reproSteps: Sign in and open Add New Monitor.
Select Kafka Producer.
Enter a Friendly Name, Topic bb-topic, and Producer Message bb.
Leave Kafka Brokers empty and click Save.

reviewedVariants.name: Kafka Producer monitor saves without any brokers
reviewedVariants.summary: The Kafka Producer editor allows a monitor with an empty Kafka Brokers list, creating an immediately unusable producer instead of requiring a broker.
reviewedVariants.expected: Save requires at least one Kafka broker and explains the missing configuration.
reviewedVariants.actual: Creation reports Added Successfully, then the monitor is Down with 'Error in producer connection: Failed to connect: brokers array is empty'. Editing and saving the empty list also reports Saved without validation.
reproSteps: Sign in and click Add New Monitor.
Select Kafka Producer and enter a friendly name.
Leave Kafka Brokers empty.
Fill Kafka Topic Name with qa-specialty and Producer Message with qa.
Click Save and inspect the monitor details.
Reopen Edit with brokers still empty and save again.

bugs.name: An obsolete DNS check overwrites healthy status after monitor configuration is changed
bugs.summary: Editing a DNS monitor while its previous check is pending starts a successful check with the new settings, but the old check's later timeout still marks the monitor Down and lowers uptime.
bugs.expected: The pending check from the obsolete port-80 configuration is cancelled or ignored; the newer successful port-53 check remains authoritative.
bugs.actual: The old check eventually reports 'queryA ETIMEOUT example.com' and changes the monitor from Up to Down although port 53 remains saved. On /dashboard/23 the successful check was timestamped18:11:23, but the later-arriving timeout was timestamped18:11:20; Last Result still showed successful records and uptime fell to50%. Reproduced separately on /dashboard/22.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a DNS monitor with hostname example.com, resolver 1.1.1.1, port 80, and heartbeat interval 120 seconds.
While the initial check is pending/Unknown, immediately open Edit, change the DNS resolver port to 53, and Save.
Open the monitor dashboard and observe Up with DNS Records from the new port-53 check.
Wait approximately 35 seconds, less than the 120-second heartbeat interval.

bugs.name: Bulk monitor deletion leaves event rows with blank monitor names
bugs.summary: Deleting monitors through dashboard Actions removes the monitors but leaves their events in the live dashboard. Their names become blank and links still point to deleted monitor IDs until reload. Individual monitor deletion clears its events correctly.
bugs.expected: Events for the deleted monitor are removed from the live dashboard, matching individual deletion and the result after reload.
bugs.actual: The deleted monitor disappears from the sidebar but its event rows remain with empty Name cells and links to the deleted ID. Reproduced for BB HTTP clone (/dashboard/21) and BB Manual (/dashboard/9). Reload removes the rows; deleting BB Push clone individually did not leave orphan rows.
reproSteps: Sign in and create a monitor, then wait for an Up or Down event to appear in the dashboard event table.
On Dashboard, use search to locate the monitor and select its checkbox.
Choose Actions > Delete and confirm Yes.
Inspect the dashboard event table without reloading.

bugs.name: Paused Push monitor still records a missing-heartbeat outage
bugs.summary: Pausing a Push monitor does not cancel its pending heartbeat timeout, so it changes to Down and records an outage while paused.
bugs.expected: A paused monitor stops checking for missed heartbeats and records no new missing-heartbeat outage while paused.
bugs.actual: The monitor still shows Resume but changes from Up to Down, records 'No heartbeat in the time window', and uptime drops to 50%. Verified on QA Push Pause Verification #16 and also observed after bulk-pausing Push monitors.
reproSteps: Sign in, add a Push monitor with a 20-second heartbeat interval, and save it.
Open its displayed Push URL in a new browser tab to send an Up heartbeat; confirm the monitor shows Up.
Immediately click Pause and confirm Yes, before the heartbeat interval expires.
Confirm the monitor action is now Resume, indicating it is paused.
Wait at least 20 seconds and reload the monitor details.

bugs.name: Monitor Save silently ignores enabled remote browser mode without a browser selection
bugs.summary: The browser monitor editor accepts Use a Remote Browser without a selected remote browser, reports Saved, then silently falls back to local Chromium after reload.
bugs.expected: Save requires a Remote Browser selection or clearly explains that remote mode cannot be enabled.
bugs.actual: Save reports Saved with the switch checked. After reload Use a Remote Browser is unchecked, and the monitor uses local Chromium. Reproduced twice.
reproSteps: Sign in, create an HTTP(s) Browser Engine monitor with a URL, and reopen Edit.
Check Use a Remote Browser.
Leave Remote Browser unselected.
Click Save and confirm the switch remains checked and Saved is shown.
Reload the editor.

bugs.name: Globalping DNS Protocol reopens as UDP after saving TCP
bugs.summary: A saved Globalping DNS monitor configured with TCP reopens in Edit with Protocol set to UDP.
bugs.expected: After saving the Globalping DNS monitor with Protocol set to TCP, its Edit form should show TCP.
bugs.actual: The create form visibly showed Protocol TCP before saving. The saved monitor appeared on the dashboard with the expected hostname, location, and AAAA record type, but its Edit form showed Protocol UDP. Waiting and reopening that same monitor again still showed UDP.
reproSteps: Start authenticated as Administrator using the supplied saved authentication session; open /dashboard and wait for monitor data to load. No credentials were entered.

Click Add New Monitor. Set Monitor Type to “Globalping - Access global monitoring probes” and Monitor Subtype to DNS. Enter a fresh unique name such as exp-globalping-dns-tcp-7m4q9k2p, Hostname example.com, and Location world.
Set Resource Record Type to AAAA and Protocol to TCP; leave other options at their defaults, then save the monitor.
Find and open the newly created monitor from the dashboard, then select Edit.
Scroll to Protocol in the Edit form. It displays UDP rather than TCP.
